name: Bank Muscat
founded: 1982 (established as Bank of Muscat; later mergers with Bank Al Ahli Al Omani and Commercial Bank of Oman; listed on MSX 1993)
ownership_summary: Listed on the Muscat Stock Exchange, with secondary listings on Bahrain Bourse and the London Stock Exchange (GDRs). At 31 Dec 2025 the largest holders were Royal Court Affairs 27.31%, Pension Funds Trust Accounts 19.55%, Ominvest Group 15.00%, Muscat Overseas Group 5.63% and Social Protection Fund 4.99%; others 27.52% (7,324 registered shareholders). The June 2026 investor presentation repeats Royal Court Affairs at 27.31%.
government_link: Yes. Royal Court Affairs holds 27.31% (31 Dec 2025 and June 2026), and the Social Protection Fund holds 4.99% (31 Dec 2025). Omani pension funds hold 19.55% through trust accounts (S2, S3). Designated a Domestic Systemically Important Bank (D-SIB) in Oman (S3).
group_structure: Single bank with a domestic Islamic window, Meethaq (CBO Islamic licence 13 Jan 2013; 31 branches at 30 Jun 2026), one branch in Riyadh and representative offices in Dubai, Singapore and Tehran (S1). The bank has no operating subsidiaries. It fully owns non-material special purpose vehicles: Muscat Real Estate Company (KSA), Meethaq Sukuk Company LLC (Oman), and BM Innovate Limited, BM SIP Limited and BM Markets Limited (Cayman Islands) (S2 p.168). It holds an associate, SICO BSC (c) in Bahrain (13.14%), which is profiled separately as bh-sico. Asset management, private equity and real estate funds, investment banking and private banking are divisions inside the bank. The Kuwait branch was closed in 2025 (S2 p.119, p.168).

subsidiaries.name: SICO BSC (c) (associate, not a subsidiary)
subsidiaries.activity: Bahrain investment bank, asset manager and broker. Accounted for as an associate.

subsidiaries.name: Meethaq Sukuk Company LLC
subsidiaries.activity: SPV that issues and acts as trustee for Meethaq sukuk

subsidiaries.name: BM Innovate Limited (Cayman Islands)
subsidiaries.activity: SPV used for fintech investments. First investment was in Zopa, a UK digital bank, in 2025.

footprint: At 30 Jun 2026: 200 branches and service centres in Oman (including 31 Meethaq Islamic branches), one branch in Riyadh, KSA, and representative offices in Dubai, Singapore and Tehran. The bank says it operates in 5 countries (6 at 30 Jun 2025). The Kuwait branch was closed in an orderly way during 2025 (S1, S2, S3).
customer_segments: Retail mass and mass-expatriate (Hisaby, launched 2025), affluent (Al Jawhar Privilege Banking), priority (Asalah Priority Banking), private banking (HNW), SME, corporate, government and GREs, institutional and financial institutions, Islamic (Meethaq).
business_lines: Segments in the H1 2026 investor presentation: Corporate Banking, Personal Banking (~4.0m retail customers; 169 conventional branches and service centres), Wholesale Banking (treasury, corporate finance, asset management, financial institutions), Meethaq Islamic Banking, and International Operations (KSA branch, SICO associate, representative offices) (S3). Wealth activities sit in several units. Premier banking (Asalah, Al Jawhar, Private Banking) sits in Personal Banking. Asset management, private equity and real estate funds sit under Investment Banking. The bank describes itself as the largest Omani mutual fund manager (S2, S3, S7, S9).

capabilities.wealth_summary: Bank Muscat has a tiered premier proposition: Al Jawhar Privilege Banking, then Asalah Priority Banking (for example OMR 30,000 in savings or OMR 3,500 monthly salary), then Private Banking for HNW clients, with an invitation-only Visa Infinite card and desks at four locations. Products include global equities, ETFs, mutual funds and bonds, offshore and portfolio management through 'reputed global counterparties', private equity and real estate funds, and tailored credit. Private banking won Best Private Bank in Oman from MEED (Dec 2025) and Euromoney (Mar 2026). In 2025 it added a private credit fund 'in partnership with one of the world's largest private assets managers' (not named) and a Life Settlement Fund. The in-house asset management division calls itself the largest Omani mutual fund manager. Its AUM was USD 3.9bn in Q4 2025 by the narrative figure, against OMR 1.36bn of funds under management in the audited fiduciary note. Funds include the Oryx Fund, the Money Market Fund (OMR 250m, the largest open-ended fund in Oman), the Al Tharwa Fund, India fund share classes and GCC real estate funds. It also offers discretionary portfolios for large clients and capital protected notes. Schroders became a strategic partner in 2021, supplying a digital risk-profiling tool and fund strategies. No investing feature was found in the retail mobile app, which was relaunched in 2025 with 200+ features. Bank Muscat holds no FSA brokerage licence.

Criteria must be met continuously. Four new Asalah Centres opened in 2025.

segments.eligibility: 'High net worth customers'; no threshold published. Visa Infinite card by invitation, credit limit from OMR 15,000. Desks at Head Office (Airport Heights), Madinat Sultan Qaboos, Azaiba and Sohar.

private_banking.detail: Private Banking for HNW clients: dedicated RMs, personalised wealth management, global equities, ETFs, mutual funds and bonds, offshore banking and portfolio management through 'reputed global counterparties', private equity and real estate funds, and tailored credit (discretionary, property, yacht and luxury car loans). Research reports are provided. Euromoney (Mar 2026) calls it 'the only player in Oman to offer a complete private banking offering', including jumbo life insurance. Award recognition: MEED Dec 2025, Euromoney 2026 and EMEA Finance 2023.

asset_management.detail: In-house division, not a separate legal entity. FSA-licensed for Investment Manager, Portfolio Management, Fund Administration, Custodian, Investment Advice and Marketing of non-Omani securities. AUM: USD 3.9bn (Q4 2025, narrative) / OMR 1,359,365k funds under management (audited fiduciary note, 31 Dec 2025). Funds: Bank Muscat Oryx Fund (MENA equities), Money Market Fund (OMR 250m), Al Tharwa Fund (income), India Dynamic Fund and India Equity Fund of Funds (Mauritius), Enhanced Fixed Income Plan, MENA Dividend Aristocrats and Emerging Markets portfolios for institutions. Private equity and real estate: Izdihar Real Estate Fund, BM GCC Property Income Fund L.P., Oman Integrated Tourism Projects Fund. Clients include pension funds, SWFs, HNWIs and corporates.

brokerage.detail: The FSA register does not list Brokerage among Bank Muscat's licensed securities activities, so it is not an MSX broker. Private Banking offers 'trading across global markets', global ETFs and bonds through an execution platform managed by RMs. The broker or counterparty is not named.

digital_investing.detail: The 2025 mobile app relaunch (200+ features, instant loans, eKYC, Themar savings plans) shows no investing feature. A 2017 'Bank Muscat Asset Management' app was informational, covering fund information and investment education. A Systematic Investment Plan of OMR 50 per month is offered, but no digital channel is stated for it.

advisory.detail: Private Banking and premier RMs give personalised wealth advice. Since 2021 an interactive digital risk-profiling tool from Schroders has been offered to eligible clients. In 2025, 87 Premier Banking RMs were training for the CISI International Certificate in Wealth & Investment Management.

discretionary.detail: The asset management division offers discretionary portfolio management to large clients, with diversified growth, trading, dividend yield and concentrated strategies. Private Banking offers portfolio management through global counterparties. The bank holds an FSA Portfolio Management licence.

model_portfolios_robo.detail: No model portfolios or robo-advice found on the bank site, in the annual report or in the presentation. The Schroders tool (2021) is for risk profiling.

funds_platform.detail: Private Banking offers global mutual funds and ETFs. Schroders' strategies were offered through a third-party dealing platform under the 2021 alliance. The platform provider is not named.

structured_products.detail: Capital Protected Notes for HNIs and institutional investors (asset management page). No terms published.

private_markets.detail: Private equity and real estate funds through Private Banking and the in-house private equity unit, which works across five jurisdictions. In 2025 the bank launched a Private Credit Fund 'in partnership with one of the world's largest private assets managers' (not named) and a Life Settlement Fund. Real estate team: sold a Dubai JBR hotel (Jan 2025) and bought Dubai Sports City property (May 2025).

islamic_wealth.detail: Meethaq is an Islamic window with 31 branches, sukuk, an IILM primary dealer role and advisory to companies seeking MSX Shari'a Index inclusion. No Shariah-compliant fund or wealth product for individuals was identified in the sources opened.

opportunities: Oman's largest asset manager (USD 3.9bn AUM in Q4 2025) and ~4.0m customers, but no investing feature was found in the retail mobile app relaunched in 2025 (S2, S3).
The June 2026 investor presentation lists 'strong growth potential in the high net worth market segment' and plans to expand asset management outside Oman (S3).

barriers: Strong in-house investment franchise: an asset management division, private equity and real estate teams, an investment bank, and FSA licences for portfolio management, investment management, fund administration and custody (S9, S10).

No FSA brokerage licence, so execution partners would be needed for any self-directed investing (S10).
Building in-house technology and AI: the Jadarah AI Academy, a Command Center and 70 concurrent projects (S2).
